alejandra (eng-security): FYI restores failing in prod for customer-77 during DR drill. Errors show KMS AccessDenied when attempting to decrypt snapshot keys. Rolling this into #incidents but surfacing here first.

tom (backup-service): Copy paste of the restore error from the restore-controller logs:
```
2026-04-04T09:12:03Z restore-controller error: Decrypt failed for snapshot 'snap-77-prod-2026-04-03T22:00Z' -> KMS:AccessDeniedException: User: arn:aws:sts::123456789012:assumed-role/restore-runner is not authorized to perform: kms:Decrypt on resource arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789012:key/zz99-yy88
```
We do see the snapshot objects exist in s3 and are still encrypted (head-object shows x-amz-server-side-encryption: aws:kms).

chao (sre): Did anything change to the key policy or grants for CMK zz99-yy88 overnight? I can pull CloudTrail/KMS logs.

kms-bot: KMS activity for key zz99-yy88:
- 2026-04-03T02:32Z: Key policy updated by role `arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/key-admin` (change id kp-332).
- 2026-04-03T02:33Z: No grants created or destroyed around that timestamp.
- 2026-04-04T08:59Z: Several Decrypt attempts returned AccessDenied for principal `arn:aws:sts::123456789012:assumed-role/restore-runner`.

alejandra (eng-security): Key policy change could have removed the `sts:AssumeRole` or the `kms:Decrypt` permission for the restore principal. chao, can you fetch the key policy diff?

chao (sre): Grabbing policy diffs now. Recent diff shows that the admin user tightened the key policy by replacing a wildcard `Principal` block with an explicit list — they removed the cross-account IAM role entry the restore-team relies on. Diff snippet:
```
-    "Principal": {"AWS": "arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/restore-runner"}
+    "Principal": {"AWS": ["arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/key-admin"]}
```
This would explain Decrypt denials.

mira (compliance): This is prod crypto material — any downtime or failed restores are high priority. We need timeline, scope (which valids/backups affected), and whether any data was exfil/downloaded while vulnerable.

alejandra (eng-security): Agreed. Immediate mitigation options: 1) Revert key policy to previous state (fastest but needs approval), 2) Create a temporary KMS grant that allows `restore-runner` to Decrypt, 3) Copy object data and re-encrypt under a different key (slow). Which is least blasty?

chao (sre): Re-creating a grant scoped to Decrypt for the restore-runner principal seems safest and lowest op blast. Grants can be created quickly and revoked after the drill. I can create with TTL 4h.

tom (backup-service): If we go grant route, the restore-controller also needs kms:GenerateDataKey or kms:Decrypt depending on encryption mode. Our controller uses GenerateDataKey for envelope keys. Confirm exact API calls in logs.

kms-bot: Audit: restore-controller performed `GenerateDataKey` calls at 09:12:03Z and received AccessDenied.

alejandra (eng-security): Okay, create a grant for principal `arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/restore-runner` with operations [Decrypt, GenerateDataKey] for zz99-yy88 TTL 4h. chao, please coordinate and post the grant UUID here. Also notify key-admin before making changes.

chao (sre): Creating grant now. Command:
```
aws kms create-grant --key-id arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789012:key/zz99-yy88 --grantee-principal arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/restore-runner --operations Decrypt GenerateDataKey --name "tmp-restore-grant-3278904567" --constraints '{"EncryptionContextSubset": {"stage": "prod"}}'
```
Response: GrantId = 6a9b-restore-grant-2026-04-04 (uuid: g-9901).

kms-bot: Grant g-9901 created at 2026-04-04T09:23Z for grantee arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/restore-runner.

tom (backup-service): Re-running the restore now.

restore-controller: info: starting restore for snap-77-prod-2026-04-03T22:00Z
restore-controller: info: GenerateDataKey successful
restore-controller: info: Decrypt successful
restore-controller: success: restore completed for customer-77 at 09:27:15Z

chao (sre): Confirmed. Restores are proceeding again for the DR drill.

mira (compliance): Thanks. Please document the exact key policy delta, the grant creation, and why the key-admin changed policy without coordinating with backups/restore owners. We'll need this in the incident record and for audit.

alejandra (eng-security): Action items:
- chao: leave the grant in place for now until postmortem and revoke after incident. Add TTL metadata and create a revoke checklist.
- tom: re-run failed restores and verify checksums for all recovered data.
- chao: collaborate with key-admin to produce a safer key policy that preserves required service principals or a process to review policy changes.
- mira: capture compliance timeline and notify stakeholders.

chao (sre): Opening INC-2026-057 and attaching key-policy-diff + grant id g-9901 + restore logs.

alejandra (eng-security): Postmortem notes to include: why key policy changes lacked coordination, add a pre-change automated test that simulates GenerateDataKey/Decrypt from the restore principal, and add a KMS change review checklist to PG.

tom (backup-service): Also adding a runtime guard in restore-controller: if GenerateDataKey/Decrypt fail, fail-fast and emit a dedicated pager to eng-security instead of queueing retries. I'll raise PR after the drill.

mira (compliance): We should also scan recent CloudTrail for any Decrypt/GenerateDataKey successes from unexpected principals in the last 90 days — want confirmation no unauthorized decrypts happened. I'll run that and report.

kms-bot: Noting: grant g-9901 scheduled TTL 4h; remember to revoke manually if postmortem recommends.

alejandra (eng-security): Thanks team. Keep updates in INC-2026-057. We'll follow up with a cross-team postmortem and policy change process. :thumbsup:
